All Out (2021) was an All Elite Wrestling (AEW) pay-per-view held on September 5, 2021, at the NOW Arena in Hoffman Estates, Illinois (Chicago area). It’s widely regarded as one of the best AEW events to date, notable for CM Punk’s in-ring return after seven years and surprise debuts by Adam Cole and Bryan Danielson.

Key facts
- Promotion: All Elite Wrestling (AEW)
- Date/venue: September 5, 2021 – NOW Arena, Hoffman Estates, Illinois
- Attendance: ~10,000 (sold-out; exact figures vary by source)
- PPV buys: Just over 200,000 worldwide (AEW record at the time)
- Reputation: Universally praised; multiple outlets and fans cite it as a top AEW PPV ever

Full card and results
Buy-In (pre-show)
- Best Friends (Orange Cassidy, Chuck Taylor, Wheeler Yuta) & Jurassic Express (Jungle Boy, Luchasaurus) def. Hardy Family Office (Matt Hardy, Private Party, TH2)

Main card
1) TNT Championship: Miro (c) def. Eddie Kingston
2) Jon Moxley def. Satoshi Kojima (NJPW)
3) AEW Women’s World Championship: Dr. Britt Baker, D.M.D. (c) def. Kris Statlander
4) AEW World Tag Team Championship – Steel Cage: Lucha Brothers (Penta El Zero Miedo & Rey Fenix) def. The Young Bucks (c) – title change
5) Casino Battle Royale (women’s): Ruby Soho won (debut; last eliminated Thunder Rosa) to earn a future title shot
6) Chris Jericho def. MJF – Jericho’s AEW in-ring career was on the line if he lost
7) CM Punk def. Darby Allin – Punk’s first match since 2014
8) Paul Wight def. QT Marshall
9) AEW World Championship: Kenny Omega (c) def. Christian Cage
   - Post-match: Adam Cole debuted, aligned with The Elite; Bryan Danielson debuted to confront The Elite

Why it mattered
- CM Punk’s return: A landmark mainstream moment that boosted AEW’s visibility and PPV buys.
- Dual shock debuts: Adam Cole and Bryan Danielson arriving minutes apart created one of the loudest closing stretches to any modern PPV.
- Match of the year contender: Lucha Brothers vs. Young Bucks (steel cage) drew rave reviews and is frequently cited among the best tag matches in AEW history.
- Business high point: The PPV set AEW records at the time for buys and helped power a strong fall TV run.
- Critical acclaim: The show was praised end-to-end; many matches earned high ratings from critics, with the tag title cage match receiving “five-star-plus” level accolades from some outlets.

Storyline notes and aftermath
- Omega vs. Christian concluded their summer program; Omega remained champion, setting up a huge non-title match with Bryan Danielson (time-limit draw) soon after on Dynamite: Grand Slam.
- Adam Cole joined The Elite immediately, strengthening the faction’s dominance.
- Bryan Danielson positioned himself as the top technical challenger to Omega.
- Ruby Soho’s Battle Royale win led to a Women’s title challenge against Britt Baker.
- Jericho ended his feud with MJF (who had previously beaten him multiple times) and continued wrestling in AEW.
- Punk’s successful return match began his run against a variety of opponents, starting with interactions against Team Taz members on TV.

Overall assessment
All Out 2021 is often considered a defining AEW event: a hot Chicago crowd, multiple memorable matches and moments, major debuts executed perfectly, and strong business results that marked AEW’s momentum entering late 2021.
